jobs.description:
Healthcare’s helping hand.

CHG shook things up in 1979 by inventing the locum tenens staffing model. We connect doctors with patients who need their care. As the largest physician staffing firm in America, our providers treat millions of patients each year.

Our industry is growing and demand is high. This means you’ll have plenty of opportunities to grow and develop in your career. Keeping healthcare healthy can be as fun as it is rewarding

The Vice President of Advisory Services provides executive leadership over CHG's Advisory Services offering and team, and serves as CHG's executive sponsor of the Client Advisory Board. This role is accountable for establishing Advisory Services as a durable, revenue-generating growth engine for CHG, and for elevating CHG's position with the largest health systems in the country from a transactional locums vendor to a strategic, trusted workforce partner. The Vice President sets the vision, strategy, and financial goals for the Advisory Services practice; leads and develops the Advisory Services team, is responsible for direct and indirect revenue growth attributed to the Advisory Services team; and personally builds and maintains C-suite relationships with Client Advisory Board members and other top health system executives, positioning CHG as a leading voice on the future of the physician and APP workforce.


This role requires a deep understanding of healthcare market dynamics, physician workforce strategy, workforce management solutions, industry best practices and standards, and the competitive advisory/consulting landscape. The Vice President works closely with Marketing, Product, Finance, Sales, and Enterprise Client Solutions leadership to align the Advisory Services offering and the Client Advisory Board with CHG's overall business objectives. This is a key executive leadership role within Enterprise Client Solutions and reports to the SVP, ECS.


Position Scope

  • Executive sponsorship of an eight-member Client Advisory Board comprising C-suite leaders from the nation's leading health systems, spanning a multi-year (18+ month) engagement arc of onsite, virtual, and digital touchpoints.
  • Accountability for an Advisory Services book of business and pipeline representing well in excess of $300M in identified opportunity spend across current and prospective enterprise health system relationships.
  • Growth and expansion of existing CHG and Advisory Services relationships in existing ECS clients, new customers and new markets. Determined by contract, team and revenue growth.
  • Identification of new products, services and market opportunities tied directly to innovation and growth.
  • Direct leadership of the Advisory Services practice, including people leaders and individual-contributor consultants; indirect influence over ECS account teams engaged in advisory-related client work.
  • Enterprise-level visibility, with regular reporting to CHG's executive leadership team (SVP, ECS and above) on advisory revenue, Client Advisory Board program health, and market intelligence.

Responsibilities

Strategic & Financial Leadership

  • Owns the Advisory Services P&L: sets and is accountable for revenue, growth, and profitability targets, including budget development, forecasting, and resource planning for the practice.
  • Defines and evolves the Advisory Services offering portfolio: analyzes market trends, customer insights, and competitor activity to identify new products, strategies, and growth opportunities.
  • Sets the long term direction for Advisory Services practice, ensuring the team develops scalable methodologies, insights, and solutions that advance client outcomes and business growth.
  • Builds a scalable Advisory Services organization by establishing the operating model, consulting methodologies, leadership capability, and knowledge-sharing practices needed to grow the business while delivering a consistent and differentiated client experience.
  • Develops and oversees the performance measurement strategy for the practice, leveraging operational and market insights to continuously improve client outcomes, business performance, and the effectiveness of advisory engagements.
  • Aligns with ECS Account Management, Business Development and divisional leaders to identify new opportunities and to execute on pilot programs, engagements and long term staffing project based work.
  • Responsible for educating and providing CHG leaders with market insights, thought leadership and new products and service models.
  • Support the identification of new and evolving competition in the market and identify weaknesses and strengths relative to CHG’s business model and offerings.
  • Influences enterprise strategy by bringing health system insights, workforce trends, and market intelligence to executive leadership, helping shape CHG's long-term products, services, and go-to-market strategy.

Client Advisory Board Executive Sponsorship

  • Serves as CHG's executive sponsor and senior-most representative for the Client Advisory Board; partners with the SVP, ECS to set the Client Advisory Board's vision, strategic agenda, and cadence across its multi-year arc, and ensures every touchpoint (virtual kickoffs, onsite meetings, digital touchpoints) delivers tangible value to members and to CHG.
  • Upholds and models the Client Advisory Board's operating principles in every session and interaction: approaches conversations industry-first, then client, then CHG; leans into hard discussions rather than avoiding them; fosters a co-creative, peer-driven dialogue rather than a CHG-led presentation; and holds CHG accountable to a 50/50 talk-time standard so the room's voice shapes CHG's roadmap.
  • Builds and maintains trusted, C-suite-level relationships with Client Advisory Board members and other top-tier health system executives (CFOs, Chief Physicians, CAOs, and system VPs); represents CHG as a physician workforce thought leader in peer forums, industry events, and executive briefings.
  • Owns the account-level strategy and "gap closure" plan for each Client Advisory Board member health system, partnering with Account Management to convert board relationships into re-engaged, expanded, or protected book of business.
  • Provides executive sponsorship and oversight of the end-to-end Client Advisory Board experience, partnering with Marketing, Executive Assistants, and cross-functional teams to ensure exceptional member engagement and flawless execution.

Team Leadership & Talent Development

  • Builds and leads a high-performing Advisory Services organization by setting the vision, operating model, talent strategy, and leadership expectations for the practice. Develops leaders who can independently lead client engagements, build executive relationships, and grow the Advisory Services business while fostering a culture of accountability, innovation, and continuous learning.
  • Builds organizational capability by coaching and developing leaders, strengthening consulting capabilities, and ensuring the practice can scale through its people rather than individual expertise.
  • Establishes clear performance expectations and resource plans for the practice, holding leaders accountable for business outcomes, client impact, financial performance, and the ongoing development of their teams.
  • Provides executive direction for the evolution of advisory delivery models and client engagement practices, enabling the team to continuously improve client outcomes, operational effectiveness, and adoption of CHG workforce solutions.
  • Fosters a culture of collaboration, innovation, continuous improvement, and knowledge sharing across the Advisory Services organization and its cross-functional partners, ensuring the team continuously evolves to meet changing client and market needs.

Cross-Functional Partnership & Governance

  • Serves as the executive voice for Advisory Services across CHG, influencing enterprise priorities through market intelligence, executive client insights, and emerging healthcare workforce trends.
  • Partners with the SVP, ECS and CHG executive leadership to align Advisory Services and the Client Advisory Board with enterprise strategy and the broader ECS go-to-market plan.
  • Collaborates cross-functionally with Marketing, Product, and Finance to build market-facing competitive intelligence, pricing strategy, and go-to-market plans for advisory offerings.
  • Establishes and monitors Advisory Services KPIs and Client Advisory Board program health metrics (member engagement, event execution, satisfaction); reports results and market intelligence to CHG's executive team.
  • Ensures legal, financial, and operational compliance for all team-negotiated contracts and statements of work.
  • Represents the organization in a variety of professional, board, and industry settings to promote the CHG brand and the value of Advisory Services.
  • Serves as an example of CHG's culture, core values, and servant leadership style.

Supervisory Responsibility: Provides executive leadership for the Advisory Services practice through the Sr. Director of Advisory Services and consulting leadership team, ensuring strong organizational performance, leadership development, succession planning, consulting excellence, and business growth across the practice. Partners in a matrixed capacity with ECS Account Management, Marketing, Product, and Finance leaders to advance enterprise objectives and deliver exceptional client outcomes.


Success Metrics

  • Advisory Services revenue, gross profit, and new-logo growth against annual plan.
  • Client Advisory Board member engagement and retention across the 18-month arc, including onsite and digital touchpoint participation.
  • Growth, retention, or re-engagement of Client Advisory Board member accounts (e.g., opportunity spend conversion, share recovery, expansion).
  • Team engagement, retention, and bench strength within the Advisory Services practice.
  • Client satisfaction and perception shift from "locums vendor" to "strategic workforce partner," as measured through CHG's annual Customer Experience Survey and Client Advisory Board member feedback.

Education & Experience

  • Bachelor's degree in business, healthcare administration, or a related field required (Master's degree preferred).
  • 15+ years of progressive experience in healthcare, consulting, or advisory services, including significant experience in sales/business development leadership.
  • Demonstrated experience building and leading executive advisory boards, councils, or similar C-suite peer forums.
  • Proven P&L ownership with a track record of driving revenue growth and achieving sales and growth targets.
  • Strong people leadership skills; proven ability to build, coach, and develop high-performing teams, including experience leading leaders and dispersed teams.
  • Deep understanding of healthcare organizations, physician workforce dynamics, industry trends, and the competitive advisory/consulting landscape.
  • Proven executive-level relationship-building and influencing skills, with the credibility to engage C-suite health system leaders as a peer.
  • Strong strategic and analytical skills, with the ability to translate business goals into specific, actionable objectives.
  • Excellent written, verbal, and executive presentation skills; comfortable presenting to and facilitating dialogue among C-suite audiences.
  • Change management and continuous improvement capabilities, including experience operating in a matrixed team environment.
  • Proficiency with CRM systems and sales enablement tools.
  • Demonstrated financial and business acumen, including budget development, forecasting, and P&L management.
  • High degree of discretion and sound judgment when handling sensitive, competitively significant, or executive-level client information.
  • Ability to travel up to 20-30% (client visits, industry events, and Client Advisory Board onsite meetings).

Preferred

  • Staffing or locum tenens industry experience.
  • Management consulting or healthcare advisory background.
  • Experience building or scaling a new business line within an established organization.
  • Experience with physician and APP workforce planning, wRVU/productivity-based staffing models, or health system operational consulting.
  • Established network of senior health system executive relationships (CFO, CMO, CAO, or equivalent).

jobs.excerpt: OverviewMacStadium is the leading managed Mac hosting solution in the world and is headquartered in Atlanta, GA.
jobs.description:
Overview

MacStadium is the leading managed Mac hosting solution in the world and is headquartered in Atlanta, GA. We offer the only enterprise-class hosting solution for Apple Mac computers, providing critical infrastructure for iOS and macOS developers at leading tech companies, big enterprises, and more. MacStadium is part of an ecosystem where apps and programs are built that are changing the way people live. It’s likely that numerous apps on your iPhone were built or tested in MacStadium’s data centers.

What we need:

The Innovation team builds the next generation of those solutions, and we are hiring an Innovation Engineer to work with our Innovation Lead on taking our macOS VDI solution to market.

The role is split about 50/50 between development and implementation and support of the product. You will build features, stand the solution up for customers, support it once it is running, and bring what you learn back into the code. If you have worked at a startup or small company where the person who wrote the feature also manages it, then you understand the environment you’ll be in.

What you will be building:

MacStadium VDI gets macOS to a distributed team quickly and securely, without the complex project work that IT and Security normally have to manage. It is in use with early stage customers now and we are taking it to GA.

The solution has a few layers, and you will work across all of them:

  • Virtualization. Virtual machines running macOS across a fleet.
  • Connectivity. Streaming technology that gets a user from wherever they are to a macOS desktop, hosted with us, their provider, or on their own hardware.
  • Management. A web console where IT builds images, creates desktops, and manages access
  • macOS. Native components and automation on the desktop itself, running on Apple silicon.
  • Identity. SSO integration with the identity providers enterprises already use.

Beyond VDI, the Innovation team is building additional emerging AI-related products that leverage Mac to deliver agents, inference, and other capabilities to customers. As VDI goes GA, your work extends into those.

What will you do:

Your time is split about evenly between building the product and getting it into customers’ hands. The two halves feed each other. Needs in a customer environment are usually the next thing you address in the product.

Development

  • Build and ship features across the stack: the streaming and connectivity layer, the web console, and native components on macOS.
  • Expand the identity and access work that expanded use cases demand.
  • Extend what is already there (reliability, updates, logging, and the monitoring a small team needs to support customers at scale).
  • Use Claude, Codex, or other AI tools for agentic development as a normal part of writing, testing, reviewing, and documenting code.
  • Automate and improve (builds, test environments, customer provisioning, diagnostics).

Implementation and support

  • Stand up early GA customers, hosted with us or in their own environment, and get them working.
  • Own the technical side of customer check-ins. Reproduce what they report, find the root cause, fix it or improve it, and close the loop with them and product.
  • Troubleshoot the full path, from the customer’s network and identity provider through to macOS on Apple silicon and the console in between.
  • Write and maintain the documentation that lets customers and the rest of MacStadium succeed without you on the call: setup guides, run books, known issues, and release notes.
  • Bring what you learn in the field back to Product and the Innovation Lead. You will have input into what gets built next.

What we're looking for:

  • 2 to 4 years of professional software engineering experience, with some of it at a product team, small company, or start up where you built, shipped, and then supported what you built.
  • Full stack, with a focus on streaming technology, modern web development, and Apple technology.
  • Strong root cause troubleshooting. You keep going past the symptom, across layers, until you can find and explain the core issue.
  • Fluency with Claude, Codex, or other AI tools for agentic development, and a habit of automating repetitive work.
  • Strong written and spoken English. You will write customer-facing documentation and explain technical problems to people who are not engineers.
  • Strong documentation and problem solving skills.

Who you are:

Assertive. You say what you think the problem is and what you would do about it, and you proactively ask for what you need.
Curious. You want to understand how the whole solution works, not just your piece of it.
Flexible. Some days you are deep in code and some days you are on a customer call, and both are the job.
An owner. You build it, you run it, and you improve it.
Good in a small, fast team. Direct feedback, early communication when something is slipping, and not much process needed to do good work.

Nice to have:

  • Experience with VDI, remote desktop, or streaming products.
  • Identity provider integrations (Entra ID, Okta, Google Workspace, or similar).
  • MDM or server management tool experience.
  • Experience with virtualization tools and technology.
  • Development of early stage products.
  • Building tools on top of LLMs or agent frameworks.

Salary Range: $100,000-$115,000

Job Description: Clinical, Microbiome & Translational Research Scientist (PhD)

Role Type: Contractor
Location: Remote (Worldwide)

We are seeking PhD-level experts in clinical research, microbiome science, and translational bioinformatics to contribute their scientific expertise to the development and evaluation of next-generation AI systems.

  • PhD in Microbiology, Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, Biomedical Sciences, Immunology, Epidemiology, or a closely related field.
  • Hands-on research experience in an academic or industry laboratory. Wet lab experience is an advantage.
  • Professional written and spoken English proficiency (C1 level or higher).

Preferred Skills and Qualifications

  • Postdoctoral or industry research experience in microbiome, clinical, or translational research.
  • Peer-reviewed publications, preferably as a first author in relevant scientific journals.
  • Experience with microbiome analysis tools such as QIIME2, Kraken2, MetaPhlAn, HUMAnN, MAG assembly and binning, or virome analysis tools.
  • Clinical and translational research experience involving TCGA, UK Biobank, biomarker discovery, survival analysis, electronic health record (EHR) and omics integration, or oncology and immunology genomics.

Job Overview:

    Clinical Team Leads (CTL) own the clinical delivery of clinical research trials. CTLs function as the Clinical Project Manager (CPM) within the core project team. CTLs partner with the Project Manager and other functional leads to ensure successful delivery of the clinical aspects of a trial within contractual and budgetary requirements. The CTL oversees the clinical and site management aspects of the trial. The CTL represents clinical delivery with the given customer.

Summary of Responsibilities:

  • Take accountability for proactively driving clinical project performance toward contracted deliverables while meeting customer needs and maintaining operational excellence.
  • Drive communication and collaboration with the client and project team across a matrixed, multicultural, environment.
  • Lead the development of the clinical project strategy and ensures prioritization with the clinical project team and key stakeholders in the creation of clear, data driven strategies and proactive management of project scope, timelines, quality and budget. In collaboration with relevant departments, prepare and deliver presentations for new business as required.
  • Manage the operational aspects of projects to support subject recruitment and retention, clinical vendor delivery and oversee the monitoring visit strategy.
  • Identify clinical project, financial and quality risks leveraging end to end risk management practices and quality by design principles.
  • Appropriately utilize data sources, dashboards and risk management strategies to drive innovation and proactive problem solving with the project and client teams.
  • Adhere to project governance and issue escalation pathways, ensuring that clinical project plans are in place to address identified risk while adhering to professional standards, SOPs, client and regulatory requirements
  • Partner with project team members and key stakeholders to oversee and manage clinical project budgets, resources and scope.
  • Ensure adherence to established budget and financial milestones. Accountable for accurately forecasting clinical project revenue and managing project costs in adherence to the budget.
  • Leading the timely management of changes to scope and the change order process. Ensures project team awareness and tracking of KPIs for any client specific metrics.
  • Provide inspiring leadership and play a key role in the creation of high performing clinical project teams. Facilitating communication and teamwork while driving delivery, ensuring that clinical team members understand contracted scope, timelines and budget.
  • Ensures that clinical resource projections are accurate and visible to resourcing teams, proactively escalating resource constraints and challenges.
  • Develops and mentors team members in multiple areas of expertise and provide feedback as needed to respective line managers
  • As required by the project roles participate and oversee the regulatory/ethics committee submissions, tracking, and documentation.
  • Support new business with active participation in Bid Defense preparation and meetings, as required.
  • And all other duties as needed or assigned

Qualifications (Minimum Required):

  • University/college degree (life science preferred) or certification in a related allied health profession (i.e. nursing, medical or laboratory technology) from an appropriately accredited institution
  • Fortrea may consider relevant and equivalent experience in lieu of educational requirements.
  • Fluent in English, both written and verbal.

Experience (Minimum Required):

  • 2+ years clinical research/monitoring experience or an equivalent combination of education and experience to successfully perform key responsibilities of the job.

  • Advanced computer skills (e.g., Microsoft Word, Excel, Project, Access and Power Point).
  • Experience managing projects in a matrix and virtual environment.
  • Excellent communication, planning and organizational skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead by example and to encourage team members to seek solutions independently Demonstrated ability to handle multiple competing priorities and to utilize resources effectively.
  • Demonstrated ability to inspire effective teamwork and motivate staff within a matrix system.
  • Financial awareness and ability to actively and effectively utilize financial tracking systems.
  • Ability to work independently and mentor junior project team members.
  • Ability to negotiate and liaise with clients in a professional manner.
  • Ability to present to staff at all levels.

Preferred Qualifications Include:

  • Master or other advanced degree
  • PMP certification 2+ years CRA experience, on-site or in-house
  • In lieu of the above minimum requirement, candidates with three or more years of relevance clinical research experience in pharmaceutical, CRO or health care setting will be considered

Physical Demands/Work Environment:

  • Standard Office Environment or remote based work required
  • Weekend and off-hour work as required

Crum & Forster (C&F) provides market leading property & casualty, accident & health, specialty and standard commercial lines insurance solutions. With our employee-first focus, the Company is consistently recognized as a great place to work, earning multiple workplace and wellness awards, including the Great Place to Work® Award, Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For, Fortune Best Workplaces for Parents, Fortune Best Workplaces for Millennials, and many others.

C&F is part of Fairfax Financial Holdings. For more information about C&F, please visit our website: www.cfins.com

Our Surplus & Specialty Lines (S&S) Division develops customized coverage solutions for complex exposures, difficult-to-insure risks and niche segments of the market. S&S has over 850 employees (including more than 250 based in India), 10+ locations in the United States and 2 locations in India. Our product reach includes Sharing Economy, Environmental, Energy, Transportation, Construction, Excess & Umbrella, Primary Special Risk, Security, and other industry segments. S&S is the second largest division within C&F at over $1.5 billion in annual gross written premium.

Job Description

Senior Agentic AI Enablement Engineer

Department: S&S Digital AI Engineering & Automation | Location: Remote, United States

Reports to: AVP, AI Engineering & Automation

Position Summary:

Crum & Forster is building an enterprise agentic AI capability across underwriting, claims, legal and compliance, and corporate operations, with engineering teams.

We are seeking a Senior Agentic AI Enablement Engineer to design, build, and ship agentic AI solutions hands-on. You will turn validated solution designs into working agents, build the reference implementations our engineering pods build on, and work embedded alongside our AI execution pods to accelerate production delivery.

This is a hands-on engineering role. Most of your time will be spent writing production-quality code: multi-agent orchestration, retrieval pipelines, tool integrations, and evaluation harnesses on AWS. You will work closely with the Principal AI Engineer, who sets architecture and technical standards, and you will be the US-based build anchor for our agentic platform.

Why This Role

You will build the agentic AI systems at the heart of C&F’s AI transformation, hands-on and on a modern AWS stack, while shaping how our engineering teams build. The role offers a clear growth path toward Principal AI Engineer as our AI capability scales.

What you will do:

Agentic Solution Engineering

  • Build multi-agent workflows across planner, retrieval, tool-calling, and validation steps, including context engineering, agent memory, state management, and escalation paths.
  • Implement autonomy boundaries, human-in-the-loop checkpoints, deterministic guardrails, and audit trails in code.
  • Develop and integrate tools and services through Model Context Protocol (MCP) and enterprise APIs, including policy administration, claims, and document systems.

Retrieval & Grounding

  • Build retrieval pipelines over unstructured submissions, claims files, and financial records: document parsing, chunking, embeddings, hybrid search, and reranking.
  • Tune retrieval quality and grounding using measurable metrics such as hit rate, MRR, and citation accuracy.

Prototyping & Reference Implementations

  • Rapidly prototype agents on Amazon Bedrock and Bedrock AgentCore to prove feasibility before production build.
  • Build reusable reference implementations, SDK components, and patterns that the execution pods adopt and extend.
  • Harden successful prototypes into production-ready components to the engineering standards set by the Principal AI Engineer.

Evaluation, Observability & Reliability

  • Build evaluation harnesses with golden datasets, LLM-as-judge scoring, and regression gates that run in CI/CD before release.
  • Instrument agents with tracing, observability, latency and cost monitoring, and work with the reliability engineering pod on production quality.

Delivery Partnership

  • Work embedded alongside the AI execution pods: pair on hard problems, review code, and unblock delivery.
  • Contribute to technical design reviews and architecture decisions with the Principal AI Engineer.
  • Mentor engineers on agentic engineering practices across US and India teams.

What you will bring t0 C&F:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field or equivalent experience.
  • 8+ years of software engineering experience, including 3+ years building Generative AI or agentic AI solutions, with at least one in production.
  • Strong Python engineering skills and experience writing production-quality, tested code.
  • Hands-on experience with LLM orchestration frameworks such as LangGraph, LangChain, or equivalent, including tool calling and multi-step agent workflows.
  • Hands-on experience building retrieval-augmented generation pipelines with vector databases, embeddings, and reranking.
  • Experience with AWS, including serverless and containerized services.
  • Experience implementing LLM evaluation and testing approaches.
  • Solid grounding in API design, CI/CD, and secure development practices.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with Amazon Bedrock, Bedrock AgentCore, Bedrock Guardrails, or Bedrock Knowledge Bases.
  • Experience building or deploying MCP servers and tool integrations.
  • Experience with agent observability and tracing tools such as LangSmith or OpenTelemetry.
  • Experience with TypeScript or another modern language in addition to Python.
  • Experience in Property & Casualty insurance or another regulated industry.
  • Experience working with distributed teams across US and India time zones.

What Success Looks Like

  • Working agentic prototypes that prove feasibility quickly and move into production build.
  • Reference implementations and reusable components adopted across the AI
  • Agents released with evaluation gates, observability, and controls built in from the start.
  • Measurably faster delivery from the engineering teams you work alongside.

What C&F will bring to you

  • Competitive compensation package
  • Generous 401K employer match
  • Employee Stock Purchase plan with employer matching
  • Generous Paid Time Off
  • Excellent benefits that go beyond health, dental & vision. Our programs are focused on your whole family’s wellness, including your physical, mental and financial wellbeing
  • A core C&F tenet is supporting your career development, so we provide a wealth of ways for you to keep learning, which may include tuition reimbursement, industry-related certifications and professional training to keep you progressing on your chosen path
  • A dynamic, ambitious, fun and exciting work environment
  • We believe you do well by doing good and want to encourage a spirit of social and community responsibility, matching donation program, volunteer opportunities, and an employee-driven corporate giving program that lets you participate and support your community

At C&F you will BELONG

If you require special accommodations, please let us know. We value inclusivity and diversity. We are committed to equal employment opportunity and welcome everyone regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, or Veteran status. If you require special accommodations, please let us know. Belonging at C&F, is a mindset. It’s about fostering a culture of inclusion and connection, where everyone feels valued, heard, and empowered to thrive and where our social impact efforts help strengthen the communities where we live and work.

Location: India - Remote

The Opportunity

At Praxis, every material movement matters. We are seeking a proactive, results-driven Manager, CMC Materials Management to own domestic and international logistics supporting our research, development, and manufacturing programs.

This role ensures critical materials reach the right destination, on time and in the required condition, while maintaining compliance, inventory visibility, and cost efficiency across our global supplier and CDMO network. The ideal candidate anticipates challenges, solves problems with urgency, and takes ownership from planning through delivery. Success requires strong execution, attention to detail, and a commitment to advancing life-altering medicines for patients.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Own end-to-end materials logistics: Plan and execute domestic and international shipments supporting CMC development, technology transfers, and manufacturing. Coordinate suppliers, carriers, freight forwarders, customs brokers, and internal teams to ensure timely, reliable delivery.
  • Ensure shipment integrity and compliance: Manage temperature-controlled shipments, packaging, monitoring, and material-specific handling requirements. Partner with Quality and Regulatory to ensure compliance with applicable procedures and promptly escalate excursions or deviations for assessment and disposition.
  • Drive accurate documentation and execution: Oversee shipping requests, including E-Transparency submissions, commercial invoices, packing lists, customs documentation, and Material Transfer Requests. Ensure complete, accurate, and timely records in the Quality Management System (QMS).
  • Maintain inventory visibility: Track and reconcile material inventories at CDMOs and external partners, monitoring stock levels, expiry dates, and availability. Coordinate replenishment and transfers to prevent disruptions to development and manufacturing schedules.
  • Manage logistics partners: Partner with Quality and Procurement to select, onboard, and oversee service providers. Support negotiations, establish performance expectations, and hold partners accountable for delivery, quality, responsiveness, and cost.
  • Anticipate and resolve risks: Proactively identify transportation, customs, storage, and supply continuity risks. Develop contingency plans, resolve disruptions with urgency, and communicate clearly with stakeholders through resolution.
  • Improve operational performance: Maintain accurate shipment and inventory records in SharePoint, Excel, and other systems. Track delivery performance, temperature excursions, inventory accuracy, and freight costs. Use data and cross-functional collaboration to simplify processes, improve reliability, and reduce avoidable costs.

Qualifications and Key Success Factors

  • Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Logistics, Life Sciences, Engineering, or related field, or equivalent experience.
  • Typically 5–8 years of experience in logistics, materials management, or supply chain operations, preferably in biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, or a regulated environment.
  • Experience managing international shipments, customs documentation, freight forwarding, and temperature-controlled logistics.
  • Working knowledge of GxP requirements, quality systems, and pharmaceutical material handling and documentation.
  • Experience coordinating inventory and material movements across CDMOs, suppliers, or external manufacturing partners.
  • Proficiency with Excel, SharePoint, and logistics or inventory management systems; familiarity with E-Transparency, QMS, or ERP systems is a plus.
  • Strong organizational skills, sound judgment, and the ability to manage competing priorities across global teams and partners.
  • Ownership: Takes initiative, follows through, and drives issues to resolution without waiting for direction.
  • Collaboration: Builds trust through clear communication, transparency, and accountability across functions.
  • Curiosity and grit: Challenges inefficient processes, anticipates problems, and delivers results in a fast-moving environment.

The physical and mental requirements of our roles include but are not limited to regular use of a computer, devices or other office equipment, clear communication, and occasional movement. You'll need comfort with screen work, basic hand coordination, and focus. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these functions.

₹2,580,000—₹2,860,000 INR

We also provide company-paid life insurance, AD&D, disability benefits, and voluntary plans to personalize your coverage. Thinking about the future?  We match dollar-for-dollar up to 6% on eligible 401(k) contributions and sweeten the deal with long-term stock incentives and ESPP.  We provide a discretionary quarterly bonus, an extremely flexible wellness benefit, generous PTO, paid holidays and company-wide shutdowns.  Not to mention, you'll also be joining a phenomenal crew of colleagues who are smart, engaged and inspiring.  We aim high, collaborate hard, and produce results.  Let’s achieve the impossible together!

Praxis Precision Medicines is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company translating genetic insights into the development of therapies for central nervous system disorders characterized by neuronal imbalance. At Praxis we share a common vision of reshaping the human condition into a more freeing and fulfilled existence by developing high impact medicines for patients and families affected by and living with complex brain disorders.   • Capacidad de resolución de problemas y toma de decisiones.

  • Comunicación efectiva y capacidad para transmitir conocimientos.

  • Trabajo colaborativo, negociación y orientación al negocio.

PROPUESTA:

  • Rango salarial: a convenir según seniority y experiencia

  • Tipo de contratación: Relación de dependencia

  • Duración del contrato: por tiempo indeterminado

  • Horario: L a V, de 7 a 16 hs

  • Modalidad de trabajo: remoto con posibilidad de encuentros eventuales en Sunchales.

DESCRIPCIÓN DEL ROL

Quien se sume al equipo tendrá un rol clave en la protección del ecosistema Salesforce y de la información de clientes, afiliados y operaciones comerciales de la organización. Será responsable de garantizar la seguridad de la plataforma mediante el diseño, implementación y auditoría continua de controles de acceso, protección de datos, desarrollos e integraciones, velando por el cumplimiento de las políticas corporativas de ciberseguridad y las normativas de protección de datos personales. Se espera que promueva una cultura de seguridad por diseño, anticipándose a posibles vulnerabilidades y asegurando que la evolución de la plataforma no comprometa la seguridad ni la agilidad operativa.

RESPONSABILIDADES:

  • Gobernar el modelo de visibilidad y control de accesos en Salesforce: Diseñar, configurar y auditar la jerarquía de roles, perfiles, conjuntos de permisos ( Permission Sets ), grupos de conjuntos de permisos ( Permission Set Groups ), valores predeterminados de la organización ( OWD - Organization-Wide Defaults ), reglas de compartición ( Sharing Rules ) y seguridad a nivel de campo ( FLS - Field-Level Security ).

  • Implementar y administrar la suite de seguridad Salesforce Shield: Configurar y supervisar los módulos de cifrado de plataforma ( Platform Encryption ), monitoreo de eventos en tiempo real ( Real-Time Event Monitoring ) y seguimiento de auditoría de campos ( Field Audit Trail ) para la protección de datos sensibles (PII/PHI).

  • Supervisar la seguridad en portales y usuarios invitados ( Experience Cloud / Sites ): Auditar continuamente las configuraciones de seguridad, permisos de usuarios invitados ( Guest User Access ), reglas de compartición pública y endpoints expuestos en portales externos para prevenir filtraciones no deseadas de información.

  • Auditar y revisar la seguridad en código personalizado (Apex / LWC):Evaluar el código fuente escrito en Apex y componentes Lightning (LWC) para detectar y mitigar vulnerabilidades como inyecciones SOQL/SOSL, violaciones de control de acceso (omisión de palabra clave with sharing o controles de CRUD/FLS en código) y vulnerabilidades de Cross-Site Scripting (XSS).

  • Gestionar la seguridad de integraciones y aplicaciones conectadas (Connected Apps):Auditar los esquemas de autenticación basados en OAuth 2.0 y SAML, gestionar los certificados, controlar los alcances ( scopes ) de las aplicaciones conectadas y verificar los conectores con el bus de integración corporativo (MuleSoft / APIs externas).

  • Ejecutar análisis periódicos con Salesforce Health Check y herramientas SAST: Realizar escaneos frecuentes de la postura de seguridad mediante Salesforce Health Check y soluciones automatizadas de análisis de código/configuración (ej. PMD, DigitSec, CodeScan), gestionando los planes de remediación técnica.

  • Garantizar la protección de datos en entornos Sandbox y procesos de Release: Definir e implementar políticas de enmascaramiento y anonimización de datos ( Data Masking ) en entornos de desarrollo y prueba (Sandboxes) para evitar el uso de datos de producción no protegidos.

  • Monitorear eventos de seguridad y apoyar en la respuesta a incidentes: Analizar logs de eventos ( Event Monitoring logs ) y métricas de comportamiento para detectar actividades sospechosas (ej. descargas masivas de informes, exportaciones anómalas o inicios de sesión desde ubicaciones no autorizadas) y colaborar con el SOC en la contención de incidentes.

  • Gobernar la instalación de soluciones de AppExchange: Evaluar los riesgos de ciberseguridad y privacidad de aplicaciones y paquetes de terceros antes de su instalación en la organización de Salesforce.

  • Gestión de políticas de sesión y autenticación en la plataforma: Configurar requerimientos de contraseñas, políticas de expiración de sesión, restricciones por rango de IP corporativo y autenticación de doble factor (MFA / Salesforce Authenticator) en coordinación con el sistema central de SSO corporativo.

  • Velar por el cumplimiento regulatorio sobre los datos del CRM: Asegurar que el almacenamiento y procesamiento de datos en Salesforce cumpla con normativas de protección de datos personales (Ley N° 25.326 de Argentina, GDPR) y regulaciones del sector salud/financiero (HIPAA).

  • Brindar capacitación técnica en seguridad de Salesforce: Entrenar a administradores, desarrolladores y consultores externos en pautas de configuración segura, desarrollo seguro en la plataforma y buenas prácticas para la preservación de datos.

jobs.excerpt: The Senior Director of Revenue Enablement & GTM AI will be an essential leader responsible for driving go-to-market (GTM) productivity, velocity, and top-of-funnel pipeline generation as SheerID scales beyond $100M+ ARR.
jobs.description:
The Senior Director of Revenue Enablement & GTM AI will be an essential leader responsible for driving go-to-market (GTM) productivity, velocity, and top-of-funnel pipeline generation as SheerID scales beyond $100M+ ARR. In this multifaceted role, you will lead two critical, interconnected engines: enterprise-wide Revenue Enablement and our AI SDR function, the AI agents that run our inbound and outbound prospecting motions alongside our human SDR team in Growth Marketing.

As an executive champion for AI transformation, you will spearhead the modernization of our revenue engine by embedding AI technologies, agentic workflows, conversational intelligence, and generative automation across prospecting and enablement programs. By connecting modern prospecting methods with continuous, role-based enablement, you will ensure our GTM teams ramp faster, engage buyers with precision, and drive predictable new and expansion bookings.

You'll own how our revenue team adopts and works alongside AI, from the tools reps use every day to the AI agents that handle inbound and outbound prospecting. You bring a point of view on what the team needs, prioritize it against company goals, and partner with Revenue Operations to build it.

Role Specific Job Duties:

AI SDR function:

  • Agentic Inbound: Own the strategy, design and results of our AI-led inbound motion: lead triage and qualification, routing, speed-to-lead, meeting confirmation and show-rate follow-up, with clear hand-off points to humans.
  • Agentic Outbound: Own the AI agents that support outbound prospecting: account research, persona and messaging, signal-based prioritization and outreach, so every SDR and AE has AI capacity behind them.
  • Human + AI operating model: Partner with Growth Marketing and Sales leadership to define who (or what) does each job, the hand-offs between agents, SDRs and AEs, and the service levels for each.
  • Outbound playbook: Own the outbound prospecting playbook used by SDRs, AEs and AI agents: account prioritization, persona messaging, channel mix and the inspection layer.
  • Tech stack and vendors: Select, implement and manage the AI SDR and prospecting tech stack, including cadence design, deliverability, data hygiene and conversion. Partner with Revenue Operations on the build.

Revenue Enablement:

  • Holistic Revenue Enablement Ownership: Design, build, and scale a comprehensive revenue enablement function supporting the entire customer journey across Sales, Customer Success, Solutions Consulting, and Partnerships, shortening ramp times, elevating commercial execution, and driving win rates.
  • AI & Tool Enablement and Adoption: Own how the revenue team adopts AI and its core tools (AI assistants, conversation intelligence, AI practice, deal and account signals, digital sales rooms). Shift routine coaching from human-led to system-led (the system flags a gap → the rep self-corrects → the manager steps in on repeat issues). Partner with Revenue Operations & Product Marketing on GTM AI training and governance.
  • Continuous Learning, Onboarding & Ramp: Architect scalable onboarding, continuous skill-building, and certification frameworks that accelerate time-to-productivity for new hires across Sales and CS while establishing clear career progression pathways from SDR into AE and CSM roles.
  • Just-in-Time Enablement & Competency Development: Move the team from scheduled training to just-in-time learning in the flow of work. Build competency frameworks for each customer-facing role, assess the team against them, and turn gaps into individual development plans. Enable front-line managers on how to coach.
  • Playbook & Methodology Institutionalization: Codify and operationalize sales methodologies (e.g., MEDDPICC, Value Selling, Command of the Message) and customer lifecycle frameworks, ensuring messaging consistency from prospecting through renewal and expansion.
  • Content Strategy & Field Feedback Loop: Own sales content strategy and governance (audit, expiry, findability, usage) and a single intake for field requests, with a clear triage and prioritization model. Turn field feedback into problem statements and decide the fix.
  • Launch, Campaign & Event Readiness: Own field readiness for product launches, pricing changes, new audiences and competitive plays. For major events and campaigns, own the pre-, during- and post-event playbooks with Growth Marketing and hold the field accountable to them.

Across both:

  • Pipeline Generation Strategy: Partner with Sales, Growth Marketing, Customer Success and Revenue Operations to shape pipeline generation strategy, aligning on how human and AI-driven prospecting work together to create one scalable engine for qualified opportunities.
  • Cross-Functional GTM Alignment: Partner closely with Sales, Customer Success, Growth Marketing, Product Marketing, and RevOps leadership to ensure enablement programs and prospecting plays align with product launches, competitive battlecards, and ICP target accounts.
  • Measurement, Analytics & Business Impact: Define and govern enablement and AI SDR performance metrics (e.g., pipeline creation, speed-to-lead, show rate, meeting-to-opportunity conversion, quota attainment, time-to-first-deal, win rate), translating program results into clear commercial outcomes.
  • Culture & Leadership Development: Foster an inclusive, high-accountability, and continuous-learning culture. Lead and develop the Senior Manager, Revenue Enablement, who owns late-cycle, renewal and expansion enablement.

What Success Looks Like (First 12 Months)

  • AI inbound motion live, with speed-to-lead, show rate and inbound conversion improving against baseline.
  • AI outbound agents supporting every SDR and AE, with measurable pipeline sourced or influenced.
  • Ramp time for new AEs and CSMs reduced, with a just-in-time enablement model in place.
  • Measurable adoption of core AI and enablement tools across the revenue team.

Required Skills / Experience:

  • Proven GTM & Enablement Leadership: 8+ years of progressive experience in revenue/sales enablement, sales leadership, and sales development within a high-growth B2B SaaS organization scaling through $50M–$100M+ ARR.
  • AI SDR & Agentic Inbound Experience: Hands-on experience designing, launching or running an AI SDR or agentic inbound/outbound program, with results against pipeline or meeting targets.
  • SDR Track Record: Demonstrated success leading or partnering closely with an outbound SDR function, with a clear history of meeting or exceeding pipeline and meeting generation targets.
  • AI Transformation Expertise: Hands-on experience identifying, piloting, and deploying modern AI tools, agentic workflows, and automation platforms, and driving real adoption across a revenue team.
  • Multi-Discipline Enablement Scope: Proven track record of building enablement programs that go beyond initial sales acquisition to include account expansion, customer retention, and technical solution readiness.
  • Modern Enablement Design: Experience building just-in-time enablement, competency frameworks and content governance, and partnering closely with Product Marketing.
  • Methodology Mastery: Deep knowledge of enterprise sales frameworks (e.g., MEDDPICC, Challenger, Value Selling) and conversational intelligence platforms.
  • Tech Stack Fluency: Deep administrative and operational fluency across the modern revenue tech stack, including Salesforce, Salesloft/Outreach, Gong, LMS/CMS enablement platforms (e.g., Highspot, Seismic, WorkRamp), data enrichment and AI SDR tools.
  • Data-Driven & Commercial Acumen: Analytical operator who connects enablement milestones and prospecting metrics directly to ARR impact, conversion velocity, and rep productivity.
  • Exceptional Communication & Executive Presence: Strong facilitation, coaching, and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to influence and partner across C-level and VP leadership.

At DraftKings, AI is becoming an integral part of both our present and future, powering how work gets done today, guiding smarter decisions, and sparking bold ideas. The Crown Is Yours

You’ll lead and grow a team of data scientists and machine learning engineers, turning complex opportunities into focused priorities and scalable solutions. In partnership with our Product, Engineering, Marketing, and Revenue teams, you’ll connect technical investments to business priorities and deliver measurable customer impact. You’ll also help shape the broader direction of our data science capabilities, raising technical standards and advancing how we approach personalization at scale.


What you’ll do

  • Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing team of data scientists and machine learning engineers, strengthening the technical and leadership capabilities needed to deliver personalization initiatives at scale.
  • Set your team’s strategy, roadmap, and priorities, translating business goals and ambiguous opportunities into high-impact data science and machine learning initiatives with clear measures of success.

  • Guide the development and deployment of machine learning systems across the full model development lifecycle, establishing rigorous standards for design, development, testing, deployment, monitoring, and iteration.

jobs.title: VP Business Development
jobs.excerpt: About PlanITROIFor more than 25 years, PlanITROI has turned retired technology into financial value for enterprise organizations.
jobs.description:
About PlanITROI

For more than 25 years, PlanITROI has turned retired technology into financial value for enterprise organizations. Our services cover IT lifecycle management, repair, refurbishment, redeployment, remarketing, reverse logistics, and secure IT Asset Disposition (ITAD). We operate on reuse-as-intended-use: reuse before recycling, and recycling only when reuse isn't viable. PlanITROI is recognized in Gartner's ITAD Market Guide and is an IAITAM Platinum Sponsor.

Our mission is to maximize the financial value of technology while extending its useful life. Every device we recover creates value for clients and gets a second life as affordable technology.

VP Business Development

PlanITROI is seeking accomplished sellers who have personally closed complex, multimillion-dollar enterprise technology contracts. Have you consistently met or exceeded a personal quota selling to Fortune 500 companies? Can you open and close major opportunities, uncover why a deal is stalled, and get the customer moving again? Can you build and coach a team while continuing to carry your own number?

If your answer to all of this is yes, we want to hear from you. If your experience is mainly managing salespeople, distributing leads, or waiting for procurement to call back, this is probably not the right role.

The opportunity

For 25 years, PlanITROI has helped enterprises extend the useful life of computing equipment through repair, refurbishment, redeployment, IT asset disposition, and value recovery. Our Fortune 500 clients are loyal advocates, with relationships averaging more than 10 years. We focus on profitable, long-term Lifecycle Services contracts within a clearly defined ideal customer profile and an addressable market exceeding $3 billion.

This newly created VP of Business Development role reports directly to the CEO and CSO. Your job is to turn qualified enterprise opportunities into signed, profitable, long-term contracts. You will start as a hands-on seller with a personal quota. As you deliver results, you will recruit, coach, and lead at least two U.S.-based enterprise sales professionals.

You will have real support

You will work closely with our CEO, CSO, Marketing team, go-to-market AI specialist, and newly formed SDR prospecting team. They will help with some generated qualified meetings, account intelligence, and sales opportunities. However, you will be expected to create your own business. Bring relationships, develop new accounts, open doors with senior decision-makers, and build pipeline beyond the leads provided to you.

What you will be accountable for

  • Own the business development process and build a simple, repeatable sales playbook and go-to-market approach. Use modern software and AI tools to manage discovery, business cases, proposals, negotiations, signed contracts, and clean implementation handoffs.
  • Build and coach a small team of business development leaders, trained to meet and exceed goals.
  • Use Challenger selling or a comparable approach to question the status quo, teach prospects something useful, tailor the business case, and secure commitments that move deals forward.
  • Restart stalled opportunities by finding the real decision-makers, understanding buying obstacles and internal politics, and agreeing on the next action needed to reach a decision.
  • Generate your own qualified pipeline while converting opportunities sourced by SDRs, Marketing, executives, and channel partners.
  • Sell across ITAD and ITAM buying groups, including C-suite executives and leaders in IT, procurement, finance, and operations. Navigate multi-site and global agreements.
  • Keep Salesforce accurate and useful. You and PlanITROI leadership should be able to see where every deal stands, what could stop it, and what happens next.
  • Own deal strategy, account-based sales plans, forecasts, next steps, follow-up, and follow-through, coordinating with Marketing on account-based campaigns.
  • Use AI, intent signals, and research tools to improve account strategy, prepare for meetings, and sell more effectively.
  • Hire and develop a U.S.-based closing team when results and economics support expansion.

What you need to have already done

  • Over the past five years, personally carried and consistently met or exceeded a meaningful new-business quota in enterprise IT hardware, IT services, software, IT asset disposition, or a closely related technology market. Be ready to show your annual quota, actual results, year-over-year growth, and how you achieved them.
  • Personally, closed several net-new multimillion-dollar enterprise contracts involving multiple stakeholders and long, consultative buying cycles. Be ready to discuss deal values, timelines, obstacles, and exactly what you did to win.
  • Managed or coached a business devlopment team, while continuing to carry a quota or held comparable player-coach responsibilities. Explain how you balance your own selling with coaching, and how you allocated opportunities fairly across the team.
  • Sold successfully to C-suite and senior leaders in IT, procurement, finance, and operations.
  • Built lead sources and partnerships through VARs, OEMs, or global systems integrators. This is a strong advantage.
  • Generate your own qualified opportunities. Be ready to explain your prospecting strategy and its results.
  • Implemented and used modern sales intelligence and AI tools in actual deals. Explain which tools you rely on and how they improve your results.
  • Demonstrated Challenger or comparably disciplined consultative selling and sound commercial judgment. Explain your sales process, ongoing training, and how you would teach that approach to your team.

How we will measure success

Our growth plan calls for a $200 million qualified enterprise pipeline and a path to $40 million in annual net-new Lifecycle Services revenue by 2028. In 2027, your first year, we expect a meaningful contribution toward our $20 million net-new revenue objective, supported by clear individual and team quotas. We will measure the massive actions that lead to profitable new contracts, lead conversion, forecast accuracy, independently sourced pipeline, and stalled deals moved to a decision.

In your first 90 days, we expect you to learn the PlanITROI way, take ownership of priority opportunities already in our pipeline, establish disciplined follow-up, build your own prospecting plan, and show how you will move stalled deals forward.

Compensation and work requirements

On-target earnings (OTE) range from $250,000 to $1,000,000+ depending on experience, performance, and the agreed compensation plan. Pay includes a base salary and substantial performance-based variable compensation. Commissions and team incentives reward profitable growth; actual earnings depend on results. We will discuss the base salary and plan mechanics during hiring.This role is designed for someone who wants to earn primarily through performance, not maximize guaranteed salary. You will work remotely from a home in the United States and must be available during U.S. Eastern Time business hours. Travel for prospect meetings, conferences, and company visits is required.

A final word

We’re not looking for someone who needs a sales organization built for them. We are looking for someone who can close business now, improve the way we sell, and build an outstanding team after proving the approach works at PlanITROI.

If that challenge excites you, tell us about the deals you have personally won and the hardest stalled opportunity you brought back to life.

PlanITROI offers a comprehensive benefits package, including health insurance, a 401(k) with company matches, paid time off, and more. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and value diversity at all levels of the organization. 

Visit our websites for more information:

PlanITROI.com | NextraTech.com | BuyRefurbished.com

Why Mozilla?

Mozilla Corporation is the non-profit-backed technology company that has shaped the internet for the better over the last 25 years. We make pioneering brands like Firefox, the privacy-minded web browser. Now, with more than 225 million people around the world using our products each month, we’re shaping the next 25 years of technology and helping to reclaim an internet built for people, not companies. Our work focuses on diverse areas including AI, social media, security and more. And we’re doing this while never losing our focus on our core mission – to make the internet better for people.

The Mozilla Corporation is wholly owned by the non-profit 501(c) Mozilla Foundation. This means we aren’t beholden to any shareholders — only to our mission. Along with thousands of volunteer contributors and collaborators all over the world, Mozillians design, build and distribute open-source software that enables people to enjoy the internet on their terms.

About the OS Integration team:

The OS Integration team ensures Firefox works well with the host operating system and environment. We’re a distributed team with expertise in Windows, macOS, and Linux-based operating systems. Our responsibilities include developing fixes and improvements for Firefox related to Windows, macOS, and Linux environments. This might include integration with a new OS feature or fixing an OS-specific user interface bug. Other responsibilities include native crash reporting, OS abstraction layers, sandboxing, hardening, updater, and enterprise DLP support.

About the role:

As a member of the OS Integration team, you’ll develop fixes, improvements, and new features for Firefox. In many cases work may be cross-platform or have a cross-platform component. This role will include maintenance and development of the installer and updater of Firefox. You’ll contribute to the team through code review and discussion.

What you’ll do:

  • Improve the quality of Firefox and other Mozilla products by debugging and fixing software defects, improving the browsing experience for hundreds of millions of users.
  • Contribute to new features and improvements.
  • Break down tasks and work with others to deliver solutions.
  • Collaborate with experienced software engineers.
  • Perform code reviews and provide technical direction.
  • Work with a geographically-distributed development team.
  • Interact with teams throughout the organization.

What you’ll bring:

  • 5+ years of overall software engineering experience
  • Strong knowledge of C and C++
  • Experience with desktop application development on Windows, macOS, or Linux with C++.
  • Knowledge of web technologies such as Javascript and HTML.
  • Knowledge of secure coding practices and memory safety concerns.
  • Strong problem-solving and debugging skills.
  • Written and verbal communication skills with a collaborative mindset.

    • Play to win

Mozilla exists to build the Internet as a public resource accessible to all because we believe that open and free is better than closed and controlled. Build scalable contracting practices through effective templates, negotiation playbooks, and risk-based review processes.


Advise the Institution: Serve as a trusted advisor to senior leadership, translating complex legal issues into clear options, practical recommendations, and informed risk decisions. Provide counsel across the OGCC's broader portfolio and lead strategic matters assigned by the SVP&GC. Represent the OGCC in key institutional, risk, and compliance initiatives while monitoring emerging developments in higher education law, particularly across AI, technology, privacy, , and cybersecurity.

jobs.excerpt: Who we are At Twilio, we’re shaping the future of communications, all from the comfort of our homes.
jobs.description:
Who we are

At Twilio, we’re shaping the future of communications, all from the comfort of our homes. We deliver innovative solutions to hundreds of thousands of businesses and empower millions of developers worldwide to craft personalized customer experiences.

Our dedication to remote-first work, and strong culture of connection and global inclusion means that no matter your location, you’re part of a vibrant team with diverse experiences making a global impact each day. As we continue to revolutionize how the world interacts, we’re acquiring new skills and experiences that make work feel truly rewarding. Your career at Twilio is in your hands.

.

Hiring and how we work

We use Artificial Intelligence (AI) to help make our hiring process efficient. That said, every hiring decision is made by real Twilions!

Also, while we are a remote-first company, you may be asked to report in person on an ad-hoc basis for team gatherings, functional off-sites or customer meetings.

.

See yourself at Twilio

Join the team as Twilio’s next Architect on our Data Substrate team

About the job

Twilio runs on data, and the platform underneath it is entering a major shift. Open table formats, the convergence of lakes and warehouses, tightening privacy regulation, and AI workloads are all changing what a data platform has to do. We’re hiring an Architect to set our direction through that shift and to make sure the systems we build over the next 3-5 years are the right ones.

You’ll own the technical strategy for our data platform, spanning storage, lake and lakehouse architecture, catalog and governance, and privacy-by-design. You’ll work across org boundaries, setting standards that dozens of teams build on and raising the technical bar for the engineers around you.

Responsibilities

In this role, you’ll:

  • Own the architecture and multi-year technical strategy for the data platform, including the lake/lakehouse, ClickHouse, Elasticsearch, and governance, and keep them coherent as one platform rather than separate systems. Define where each engine fits (for example, ClickHouse versus open table formats on object storage) and the migration path between them.
  • Make and document the major design decisions (ADRs, RFCs) on storage and open table formats, catalog strategy, compute engines, tenancy, data placement, and build-versus-adopt tradeoffs, with cost and performance at petabyte scale as explicit design constraints.
  • Set the reference architectures for how our core storage and query engines (ClickHouse, Elasticsearch, and lake engines) are deployed, tuned, scaled and operated as shared platforms, including capacity, cost, tenant isolation, and upgrade strategy.
  • Define the reliability model for the platform: availability targets, failure domains, disaster recovery, observability, and incident response patterns that teams can adopt.
  • Build privacy and compliance into the architecture, not onto it. Design deletion and right-to-erasure, retention, data residency, and PII classification so they work across the platform’s storage layers, backups, and derived datasets, including data that arrives from upstream streaming systems.
  • Drive data governance: classification, catalog and metadata, lineage, access control integrated with our authentication and authorization systems, data contracts, quality and integrity standards, and a catalog teams actually use.
  • Review designs and technical direction across the org, and act as the escalation point on hard distributed-systems and performance problems.
  • Mentor principal and senior engineers, and grow architectural judgment across the org, not only within one squad.
  • Partner with product, security, infrastructure and consuming teams to turn business needs into platform roadmaps, and say no or re-sequence when the tradeoffs require it.
  • Track emerging data technologies (such as streaming-first architectures, federated query, and AI-ready data layers) and bring forward the ones worth adopting, with evidence from prototypes or benchmarks.

Qualifications

Twilio values diverse experiences from all kinds of industries, and we encourage everyone who meets the required qualifications to apply. If your career is just starting or hasn't followed a traditional path, don't let that stop you from considering Twilio. We are always looking for people who will bring something new to the table!

Required:

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 15+ years of experience in software development or a related field, with at least 8 years in an architecture or senior technical leadership role.
  • Proven track record of architecting and delivering large-scale data platforms and setting their technical strategy, on cloud infrastructure such as AWS, deployed with Kubernetes, Terraform and Helm.
  • Deep expertise in storage and compute for analytical data: columnar and open table formats, lake and lakehouse architecture, partitioning, indexing, query planning, and how the choices affect cost and performance at petabyte scale.
  • Breadth across data storage and retrieval technologies, with hands-on depth in at least two of: analytical/OLAP engines (e.g., ClickHouse), search engines (e.g., ElasticSearch/OpenSearch), and lake or distributed processing engines (e.g., Spark, Trino, Flink). You can reason about when to use each, how they interoperate, and how to migrate between them.
  • Working knowledge of streaming systems (e.g., Kafka) and how they interact with downstream storage.
  • Practical experience designing data governance at scale: data classification, catalog and metadata management, lineage, and access control integrated with authentication and authorization systems.
  • Practical experience implementing privacy and compliance requirements (deletion, retention, residency) across a large, heterogeneous data estate.
  • Proficiency in one or more of Python, Java, and Go.
  • Track record of writing and driving architecture decisions across multiple teams, and of changing the direction of an organization’s technical roadmap through influence rather than authority.
  • Experience elevating engineering standards and mentoring senior engineers across teams.
  • Demonstrated commitment to operational excellence: architecting for high availability, observability and incident response in distributed systems, and being credible when a platform is failing in production.
  • Strong written and verbal communication, including making a complex tradeoff clear to engineers and to senior leadership.

Desired:

  • Experience operating one of these engines (e.g., ClickHouse, ElasticSearch) at scale, including replication, sharding, ingestion behavior, and multi-tenant isolation.
  • Experience with catalog and metadata systems (e.g., Unity Catalog, Glue, Polaris, DataHub) and open table format catalog strategy.
  • Experience with a platform migration across domains or ownership models, such as moving from central to domain-owned data.
  • A track record of measurable cost optimization on large data platforms.
  • Networking and network security knowledge.

Location

This role will be remote, and based in the United States.

Travel

We prioritize connection and opportunities to build relationships with our customers and each other. For this role, you may be required to travel occasionally to participate in project or team in-person meetings.

What We Offer

Working at Twilio offers many benefits, including competitive pay, generous time off, ample parental and wellness leave, healthcare, a retirement savings program, and much more. Offerings vary by location

Compensation

*Please note this role is open to candidates outside of California, Colorado, Hawaii, Illinois, Maryland, Massachusetts, Minnesota, New Jersey, New York, Vermont, Washington D.C., and Washington State. The information below is provided for candidates hired in those locations only.

The estimated pay ranges for this role are as follows:

  • Based in Colorado, Hawaii, Illinois, Maryland, Massachusetts, Minnesota, Vermont or Washington D.C. : $207,200 - $233,100.
  • Based in New York, New Jersey, Washington State, or California (outside of the San Francisco Bay area): $219,360 - $246,780.
  • Based in the San Francisco Bay area, California: $243,680 - $274,140.

This role may be eligible to participate in Twilio’s equity plan and corporate bonus plan. All roles are generally eligible for the following benefits: health care insurance, 401(k) retirement account, paid sick time, paid personal time off, paid parental leave.

The successful candidate’s starting salary will be determined based on permissible, non-discriminatory factors such as skills, experience, and geographic location.

Application deadline information

Applications for this role are intended to be accepted until 1/4/2027 but may change based on business needs.

Twilio thinks big. Do you?

We like to solve problems, take initiative, pitch in when needed, and are always up for trying new things. That's why we seek out colleagues who embody our values — something we call Twilio Magic. Additionally, we empower employees to build positive change in their communities by supporting their volunteering and donation efforts.

So, if you're ready to unleash your full potential, do your best work, and be the best version of yourself, apply now! If this role isn't what you're looking for, please consider other open positions.

.

Stay alert to recruitment fraud

We care about your safety. Scammers sometimes impersonate Twilio recruiters through fake job postings, emails, websites, or messages. Please ensure you are engaging with an official @ email address. We will never ask for payment, gift cards, cryptocurrency, or banking information during the recruiting process. We do not make job offers without a formal interview process or conduct interviews exclusively through text-based messaging apps.

.

Twilio is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, reproductive health decisions, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, genetic information, political views or activity, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. We also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state and local law. Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment in accordance with the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers and the California Fair Chance Act. Additionally, Twilio participates in the E-Verify program in certain locations, as required by law.

jobs.description:
Overview

Who We Are

Because health is personal. That's why Personify Health created the first and only personalized health platform—bringing health plan administration, holistic wellbeing solutions, and comprehensive care navigation together in one place. We serve employers, health plans, and health systems with data-driven solutions that reduce costs while actually improving health outcomes. Together, our team is on a mission to empower people to lead healthier lives.

Learn even more about the work that drives us at personifyhealth.com.

Responsibilities

Ready to turn complex medical journeys into clear plans and better outcomes?

Why This Role Matters

When a member faces a serious diagnosis or a difficult recovery, they need someone in their corner who knows the system and can make it work for them. That’s you. As a Case Manager, you’ll assess the whole person, build care plans that fit their life, and connect them with the providers and programs that move them forward. Your clinical judgment improves outcomes while ensuring care is used appropriately and costs stay in check. You’ll also guide LVNs and LPNs on complex cases and set the standard for documentation and compliance. When you do this well, members get better care and the organization earns the trust that keeps our programs strong.

What You’ll Actually Do

  • Manage cases by phone: Lead short- and long-term cases in line with company guidelines, policies, and industry criteria (NCQA, CMSA, URAC), keeping members moving toward their goals.
  • Assess the whole person: Conduct comprehensive biopsychosocial assessments covering physical, emotional, psychosocial, spiritual, environmental, and financial factors so every care decision starts with the full picture.
  • Find the story in the claims: Use claims-processing tools to review paid claims, identify health trends, and determine eligibility for case management programs.
  • Build and refine care plans: Develop and update individualized treatment plans for standard and catastrophic cases with measurable short- and long-term goals.
  • Prove the impact: Evaluate intervention effectiveness and document measurable outcomes that show clinical impact and cost savings.
  • Keep everyone connected: Maintain continuous communication with members, caregivers, providers, employers, and the multidisciplinary team throughout the course of care.
  • Advocate for quality and value: Champion quality patient care while supporting appropriate utilization and reducing overall healthcare costs, and refer members to chronic disease, wellness, behavioral health, and vendor-specific programs as needed.
  • Drive cost management: Implement cost management strategies and document results in case management reviews and cost-avoidance reporting.
  • Support utilization review: Assist with Utilization Review for assigned members to keep care appropriate and well coordinated.
  • Mentor and guide: Coach LVNs and LPNs and support complex case guidance within licensure scope.
